newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-EDBERG ENDS QUALIFIER'S RUN AS MORE SEEDS TUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG ENDS QUALIFIER'S RUN AS MORE SEEDS TUMBLE.

text.p: Stefan Edberg recovered from one set and 3-2 down to beat Dutch qualifier Fernon Wibier 4-6 6-4 6-2 and reach the Paris Open quarter-finals on Thursday amid a continued tumbling of seeded players.

The 1990 Bercy champion, who retires at the end of the season, was unsettled by Wibier's aggression as the little known 25-year-old Dutchman upstaged the Swede at his own net game in the third round match on the Bercy centre court.

But Edberg, reluctant to bring down the curtain prematurely on a long-standing love affair with the Parisian tennis crowd, dug into his reserves to reply to Wibier's cheeky break of service in the fifth game of the second set by breaking right back to level at 3-3.
From that point in a match lasting 74 minutes, the 211th ranked Wibier was allowed only another three games, Edberg clinching it with a deft lob on his first match point.
"You never know what to expect nowadays. He surprised me a bit and I got myself into trouble, I missed easy volleys and wasn't very pleased with myself," Edberg said.
"When I got the break point it was a different match from then on.
"I'm happy to be left in the tournament, it's a bit like Wimbledon (with so many seeds gone). It would have been a missed opportunity. I'm playing well enough to get a good result here this week."
Three more seeds fell in the first three third round matches, bringing the total to 12 since nine crashed out in the second round, including holder and top seed Pete Sampras.
Marc Rosset, conqueror of Sampras on Wednesday, recovered from twisting his ankle early in the third set to beat 16th seed Felix Mantilla of Spain 7-5 3-6 7-6.

The 1994 finalist, who had three minutes treatment after falling as he made the shot that gave him a 2-0 led in the decisive set with a break of Mantilla's service, said: "I have no problem with my ankle now. I just stopped to see if I needed a bandage."
Wimbledon semifinalist Todd Martin, seeded 11, was ousted by Dutchman Paul Haarhuis 6-4 3-6 7-6.

Haarhuis, ranked 29 in the world, recovered from 4-2 down in the tiebreak to take it 7-4 on his first match point with a fine passing shot. It was the Dutch doubles specialist's first win over Martin in four meetings.
Earlier, number eight seed Wayne Ferreira crashed out 6-2 6-4 to Swede Magnus Gustafsson, who he has never beaten in three meetings including the third round at Wimbledon this year.
The South African lasted just 59 minutes on centre court against the player who on Tuesday eliminated number nine seed Andre Agassi.

The result secured Boris Becker, upset by Spain's Carlos Moya in the second round on Wednesday, his berth in the eight-man ATP Tour World Championship in Hanover next month, where he will defend the title.
He is in sixth place with Agassi and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek currently occupying the last two berths.

ATP Tour officials said Ferreira and Martin, scheduled to play in Stockholm next week along with Becker, were all but mathematically out of the running for the year-end event formerly known as the Masters.
